headline: Page-group size in bytes does not imply or guarantee a fixed token block size; token block size depends on model dimensions and tensor parallelism
claim: Author boundary: the paper reports Table 8 as a conversion from page-group size to tokens per page-group; it does not claim a byte size is universally equivalent to vLLM's 16-32 token block size. Inferred consequence: comparing page-group bytes to token block size requires normalization by model and TP configuration.
paper_fact: Table 8 shows the block size i.e., number of tokens per physical page-group. Smaller page-groups enable fine-grained allocation, approaching vLLM’s recommended block size of 16–32
premise: KV cache bytes per token per layer is H*D*P; tensor parallelism splits KV heads; page-group bytes divided by per-token bytes gives tokens per page-group.
inference: Therefore, a page-group size in bytes is not a token block size; the same byte size maps to different token counts across models and TP degrees.
conditional_consequence: If comparing fragmentation granularity to vLLM's 16-32 token block size, convert using H, D, P, and TP; otherwise the comparison is not apples-to-apples.
critical_link: The conversion from bytes to tokens is the link between allocation granularity and fragmentation granularity; without it, page-group size cannot be compared to block size.
necessary_conditions: model H, D, and P are known
page-group size is specified in bytes
per-token footprint calculation is valid for the layout
no tensor slicing or multi-layer page-group changes the layout
defeaters: tensor slicing across layers changes effective block size
different KV cache layout or precision
kernel block size differs from allocation granularity
TP changes the number of KV heads per worker
do_not_infer: page-group size alone determines block size
Table 8 values are universal across models and TP degrees
vLLM block size is directly comparable to bytes

headline: Reducing fragmentation to 1/N does not imply proportional end-to-end memory or batch-size benefit
claim: The reported 1/N fragmentation reduction is relative to the prior per-layer 2MB-page design, not a guarantee that total GPU memory use or batch size improves by a factor of N.
paper_fact: This reduces fragmentation to 1/𝑁of the prior design as shown in Table 10.
premise: Fragmentation is only one component of GPU memory use; total memory also includes model weights, activations, allocator overhead, and other allocations, and batch size depends on the total.
inference: Inferred consequence: a 1/N reduction in per-request page waste does not by itself establish a 1/N reduction in total memory or a 1/N increase in batch size.
toy_example: Toy example (not a measurement): if N=32 and per-layer 2MB-page waste is 1MB per request, slicing reduces that waste to about 32KB per request; this does not mean total GPU memory falls by 32x because weights and other allocations remain.
conditional_consequence: If fragmentation is the dominant memory constraint and N is large, the slicing benefit can approach the reported 1/N page-waste reduction; if other memory dominates or N is small, the end-to-end benefit is limited.
critical_link: The share of total GPU memory and batch-size limits attributable to per-layer 2MB-page fragmentation.
necessary_conditions: fragmentation is a dominant share of total GPU memory
N is large enough that 1/N page waste is small
page waste per request is significant
batch size is limited by KV-cache fragmentation rather than other memory
defeaters: request lengths align with page boundaries
do_not_infer: Do not infer total memory or batch size scales by N; the paper's 1/N is fragmentation relative to the prior per-layer 2MB design.
Do not infer the authors measured an end-to-end 1/N gain; Table 10 reports block sizes.
Do not infer slicing removes all fragmentation; it reduces the prior design's fragmentation to 1/N.

quotes.quote: This reduces fragmentation to 1/𝑁of the prior design as shown in Table 10.
In this method, we use a single 2MB page to store the KV cache tokens of all layers for a given request.

This can be done by allocating one virtual tensor of shape [𝐵, 𝐿, 𝑁, 𝐻, 𝐷] for K cache (and one for V cache) and slicing it across all layers, instead of allocating 2×𝑁virtual tensors of shape [𝐵, 𝐿, 𝐻, 𝐷].

author_boundaries: Authors report 1/N fragmentation relative to the prior design and Table 10 block sizes; they do not report a 1/N end-to-end memory or batch-size gain.
